title: Separate setup helpers from VCS shim
rationale: Dispatcher setup/install behavior is stack-specific setup logic rather than VCS branching logic, so it should live outside the git compatibility shim.

name: Tighten QA/finalize validation loops
description: Developer prompt now forbids unrelated test copying, QA reports must include npm test command/count evidence, and finalize distinguishes modified-file failures from pre-existing unrelated failures so branch-ready is blocked without wasting a developer retry.

name: Finalize phase outputs
description: Finalize now uses FINALIZE_VALIDATION.md as the workflow verdict artifact while still writing FINALIZE_REPORT.md for operational push/rebase details.

title: Refinery jj rebases must stay on the backend path
rationale: Refinery previously ran raw git rebase <target> <branch> from the repo root even in colocated jj repos, which broke the branch-ready invariant by validating one merge path in finalize and a different path in refinery. Rebased jj runs should go through VcsBackend.rebase() in the run workspace so finalize and refinery share backend semantics.

title: Finalize failure must not infer success from missing mail
rationale: agent-worker onPipelineComplete previously treated missing finalize phase-complete/agent-error mail as success, which allowed finalize FAIL verdicts to enqueue merge work and reach refinery. The worker must preserve the pipeline success=false result when finalize mail is absent.

name: Keep orchestrator tests aligned with runtime validation contracts
description: Pipeline epic tests need QA fixture reports with npm test command text and pass/fail counts so qaReportHasTestEvidence() treats PASS/FAIL verdicts as valid. Refinery migration tests should assert backend mergeWithoutCommit()/getConflictingFiles() behavior rather than raw git --squash shell calls.

title: Ignore detached HEAD branch labels for dispatch and merge targeting
rationale: Detached workspaces can surface HEAD as the current branch, but branch:HEAD is not a real merge target. Rejecting it at branch-label extraction/application prevents dispatcher from persisting stale branch:HEAD labels and makes refinery fall back to the real default or explicit target branch instead of failing the no-commits guard against HEAD.

title: Skip branch-ready when troubleshooter already landed the branch
rationale: A finalize failure can still be recoverable by the troubleshooter, but if that recovery directly lands the work on the target branch, enqueueing the run to merge queue and emitting branch-ready causes a false no-commits merge failure. After troubleshooter recovery, agent-worker should detect zero diff versus the target branch, close the task, and skip merge queue / branch-ready.

content: Troubleshooter prompts and tool-facing JSON should use task/taskId terminology. Keep legacy taskId only as a compatibility alias for internal runtime fields and older tool callers, not as the primary language shown to agents or operators.

description: In colocated jj repos, JujutsuBackend.detectDefaultBranch() and getCurrentBranch() cannot rely on main/master or raw working-copy change IDs. During a dirty working copy on dev, getCurrentBranch() returned the unbookmarked jj change ID (for example yozrpnkmlxpq), and run/auto-merge threaded that into merge targeting. Refinery then reported no-commits against the change ID instead of the real trunk.
resolution: Honor git-town.main-branch and origin/HEAD before bookmark-name fallbacks in detectDefaultBranch(), and in getCurrentBranch() fall back to the parent revision's bookmark before returning a jj change ID.

title: Finalize pre-existing test failures should reconcile to merged when already landed
rationale: A finalize verdict of tests_failed_pre_existing_issues does not necessarily mean the task failed to land. In jj/git workflows the branch may already match the target branch by the time finalize reports the deterministic failure. In that case agent-worker should mark the run merged and close the task instead of recording a failed run that contradicts repository state.

description: Finalize retry suppression depended on parseFinalizeFailureScope(), but the parser only recognized inline '## Failure Scope: ...' or plain '- UNRELATED_FILES' formatting. Real finalize artifacts used section formatting with bold bullets ('## Failure Scope' then '- **UNRELATED_FILES**'), so the parser returned unknown and pipeline-executor incorrectly sent Finalize Feedback - Retry N back to developer.
resolution: Accept bold bullet section formatting in parseFinalizeFailureScope() so UNRELATED_FILES is recognized from real finalize artifacts and finalize does not re-enter the developer/QA loop for pre-existing unrelated failures.

title: Finalize only reruns validation on target drift
rationale: QA already validated the task; finalize should only rerun npm test when the target branch revision changed after QA. Persisting QA target/head refs in run progress lets finalize distinguish no-drift pushes from true drift verification.

title: Finalize integration uses intent-based command naming
rationale: The finalize step is meant to bring target-branch drift onto the task branch for validation, not to prescribe rebase as the architectural policy. Renaming FinalizeCommands.rebaseCommand to integrateTargetCommand and the prompt variable to vcsIntegrateTargetCommand keeps backend behavior flexible while matching finalize's real purpose.

title: Finalize skip-vs-rerun is runtime-enforced
rationale: Pipeline-executor now records the current target ref before finalize verdict handling and validates FINALIZE_VALIDATION.md against the drift expectation. If target refs match, finalize must mark Test Validation as SKIPPED; if target drift exists, finalize may not skip validation. This prevents prompt drift or agent mistakes from bypassing the finalize drift contract.

title: JJ head resolution should ignore ephemeral scratch children
rationale: In colocated jj repos, bookmark moves and git-imports can leave the default workspace on an unbookmarked empty child commit while the real branch tip sits on @-. JujutsuBackend.getHeadId() now prefers the parent change when @ is unbookmarked but @- carries bookmarks, so finalize/refinery runtime checks reason about the effective branch tip instead of the scratch working-copy child.

description: A live bd-ca19 rerun showed '[foreman] Auto-labeled bd-ca19 with branch:HEAD' even after earlier branch-label sanitization work. Dispatcher was still detecting currentBranch through a raw GitBackend path before workspace creation, which returned detached HEAD in this colocated jj repo.
resolution: Use VcsBackendFactory.create({backend:"auto"}) for dispatch-time branch detection and reject invalid branch labels like HEAD before auto-labeling.

description: Finalize retry suppression missed artifacts that used '## Failure Scope Analysis' with '### Classification: UNRELATED_FILES'. That caused no-drift finalize contract failures with unrelated test failures to loop back to developer even though the failure was meant to be terminal/non-retryable.
resolution: Extend parseFinalizeFailureScope() to recognize analysis/classification forms and cover the case with a pipeline retry regression test.

description: Finalize can fail on unrelated rebase conflicts when a task commit contains transient artifacts like TEST_RESULTS.md.
resolution: If the task branch is unpushed, save the intended diff, reset the task branch to origin/main, reapply only the intended task files, recommit, then rebase/push to verify finalizeability.

description: Validate external CRD/API objects against the real API server before trusting mock-backed tests: a hand-written mock accepts shapes the server rejects. Four invalid shapes passed unit tests here — a kelos Task missing required 'credentials', volumes at spec.volumes instead of spec.worker.podOverrides.volumes, TaskBudget.spec.period as a string instead of an object, and workerPoolRef combined with mutually-exclusive fields. Each was caught only by 'kubectl apply --dry-run=server' against the installed CRD. Same class as stubbing a VCS: the stub accepted a bare branch name where real git needs origin/<branch>, and a conflictingFiles field that does not exist on MergeResult.
resolution: Dry-run every generated object against the live CRD (kubectl apply --dry-run=server) before relying on unit tests, and exercise VCS seams against real repositories in an integration test. Encode each discovered constraint so it cannot regress: make the field required in the options type rather than optional, and cite the dry-run in a comment on the assertion.

description: A crashing Elixir GenServer reports its failure as the ABSENCE of activity, not as an error. ForemanServer.Scheduler.age_seconds/2 clause-matched nil/DateTime/binary but not NaiveDateTime, which is what the Postgres read model returns for updated_at — so every 5s tick raised FunctionClauseError in active_runs/0 and terminated the process. Two tells both pointed away from the real cause: the /scheduler/tick endpoint returned 500 with an EMPTY BODY, and scheduler state reported last_tick: nil, which reads as 'never started' rather than 'dies on every tick'. coerce_datetime/1 in projection_store.ex already handled the naive case, so this was a missed clause on a known shape.
resolution: Add the %NaiveDateTime{} clause reading the value as Etc/UTC. When a scheduler or poller appears idle, read the server logs for a GenServer terminating before believing it never ran; and when one datetime helper handles a shape, grep sibling helpers for the same clause set.

description: A capacity/slot accounting bug can hide behind a health flag that is computed but never consumed. ForemanServer.Scheduler counted ALL active_runs toward max_concurrent while the 'stale' flag it already calculated went unused, and nothing sweeps stale runs (RecoveryEngine only reconciles an observation pushed to it, it never polls) — so an abandoned run's slot was never released and dispatch silently stopped. The subtlety that makes the naive fix wrong: WorkerHeartbeat does NOT bump run.updated_at (only phase transitions do), so a single long phase looks stale by timestamp while its worker is alive. On the live cluster a dead run read updated_at ~42m but heartbeat_age 12.4h.
resolution: Count capacity over live runs only, but judge staleness on heartbeat age with updated_at as fallback, and keep reporting every active run so stale ones stay visible. When a projection already computes a health/stale flag, grep for its consumers — a flag with no reader is a bug waiting to surface.

description: A failing step that does not BLOCK is the hardest kind to notice. Foreman's Node assumption had four sites; three were found one at a time by live runs. The fourth (npm ci + npx tsc --noEmit in the finalize builtin) survived all three rounds because it only wrote 'FAILED' into FINALIZE_REPORT.md without failing the pipeline — so every non-Node report carried two false failures indistinguishable from real ones. Related: npm ci REQUIRES a lockfile (fails on manifest-only Node projects), and npx tsc without a tsconfig.json tries to FETCH a package rather than typecheck.
resolution: Skip inapplicable steps and report SKIPPED, not SUCCESS, so 'nothing to do' stays distinguishable from 'passed'. Write the end-to-end test across ALL sites of a shared assumption at once, and pin the opposite direction too — a skip-everything implementation satisfies every negative assertion.

name: probe-projection-shape-for-event-sourced-fixtures
description: When writing a test fixture against an event-sourced projection, probe the resulting projection shape instead of trusting the event payload you wrote. Two Foreman examples that each silently produced a fixture testing nothing: RunFailed stamps run.failed_at from the EVENT's occurred_at and ignores a payload failed_at, so backdating via payload records every failure as 'now' (expiry untestable); and a run's task_id is populated only by RunStarted, so a run recorded via RunFailed alone is not attributable to its task, making a 4-failure fixture count as 1 and computing the wrong backoff window. Fix: write a throwaway test dumping Map.keys/values of the projection entry, build the fixture from what is actually stored, and emit the same event sequence a real run does (RunStarted before RunFailed) rather than only the terminal event.

When a layered prompt injects guidance that contradicts the shared prompt it wraps, the later and more specific instruction wins - and a stronger model can mask the conflict entirely by resolving it correctly. A kelos documentation phase went STUCK on a missing DOCUMENTATION_REPORT.md because the report-shim guidance ('Foreman's reports directory is not writable, upload instead') was placed BEFORE the phase prompt, which then said: Create the directory first with mkdir -p "{{reportDir}}". MiniMax obeyed the mkdir, hit 'mkdir: cannot create directory /home/foreman: Permission denied', announced it would look for the shim, and never issued the call - reporting the phase blocked. claude-haiku had resolved the identical conflict correctly (it called the shim 3x), so the failure read as MiniMax flakiness. It was not: the run that passed was a different workflow (nodeless pins documentation to Haiku; smoke and default both pin it to MiniMax). Model-correlated intermittency in prompt-driven behavior is a conflict signal, not flakiness - diff the workflow's model pins before blaming the model.
resolution: Append injected guidance AFTER the wrapped prompt so it is the last word, and have it NAME and overrule the specific conflicting instruction ('ignore any instruction above telling you to mkdir -p that directory') rather than hinting indirectly that the directory is unwritable. Also state that the expected error is not a blocker, or the agent reports the phase blocked on seeing it. Fix in the INJECTING seam, not the shared prompt, when the shared text is correct for its other consumers: reportDir is real and writable on the local path (pi-sdk-tools ensureReportDir mkdirs it) and prompt-loader REQUIRED_PROMPT_MARKERS pins {{reportDir}}/DOCUMENTATION_REPORT.md, so deleting the line would break local runs to fix pod runs. Verify by asserting RELATIVE ORDERING in the assembled Task.spec.prompt, and teeth-check the ordering assertion and the wording assertion INDEPENDENTLY - reverting one must fail only its own test, or one assertion silently covers the other's seam.
